relations.subject: Akira Takeda
relations.evidence: He served as a professor at the College of Arts and Sciences at the University of Tokyo and later held the titles of professor emeritus at both the University of Tokyo and Meikai University.

relations.subject: Akira Takeda
relations.evidence: He later taught at Tokyo Woman's Christian University and then at Meikai University, where he was also awarded the title of professor emeritus upon retirement.

relations.subject: Akira Takeda
relations.evidence: In the spring of 1949, he entered the University of Tokyo... In 1953, he graduated from the Faculty of Letters at the University of Tokyo with a degree in Chinese literature.

relations.subject: Akira Takeda
relations.evidence: In 1959, after completing the coursework for the doctoral program in Chinese language and literature, he withdrew without earning a doctorate.

relations.subject: Akira Takeda
relations.evidence: Upon advancing to the doctoral program, his academic advisor, Takejiro Kuraishi, instructed him to resign from the baseball team to focus solely on research.

relations.subject: Akira Takeda
relations.evidence: In 1961, he was appointed as an assistant at the University of Tokyo's Faculty of Letters.

relations.subject: Akira Takeda
relations.evidence: From 1965 onward, he held positions as lecturer, associate professor, and professor at the College of Arts and Sciences... In 1991, he retired upon reaching the mandatory retirement age
